revision: aa1ca3d + ACK-buffer counter; treatment changes ACK_BUFFERS from 4 to 16
notes: Matched normal release builds; both include the production retained DATA suffix and the new ack_buffer_drops counter. No ACK packing, offload-floor or control-rate changes.
Treatment changes ACK_BUFFERS from 4 to 16; the existing dependent incoming/outgoing queue capacities and startup accounting change with it. No turn-budget or ACK-policy change.
ack_buffer_drops counts ACK records rejected for lack of reserved incoming ACK storage and is ALREADY INCLUDED in queue_drops. It is not an additive drop category.
Both builds pass 339 ordinary release tests, 16 sender kernel tests, all-target/all-feature musl Clippy -D warnings and formatting. No full routed PMTU test for the buffer-size experiment.

Each build runs four retained-daemon 20-second points; no builds or other tests overlap load. Larger pool removes this rare loss but goodput changes are mixed across paced/unlimited/return points. Production retains four buffers.
All eight observations pass zero outer-fragmentation, outer/inner socket-error, admission-pressure and malformed/invalid/duplicate/out-of-window/wrong-run/reordering checks.

Directions L->R/R->L, endpoint arrays L/R. Goodput excludes drain, missing ratios include drain. 100% CPU equals one core. TAP SKBs, expired frames and queue entries cannot be summed into exact frame loss.
